messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: SEV2 - synthetic-prober-eu-west surge. Alert summary: 70% probe failures for 'canary-prober-eu-west' over 2m (timeout/conn-reset). PD incident: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD12345

pagerduty-bot: Incident created and paging rotation. Escalation policy: synth-prober-oncall -> sre-rotation.

Devon: ack'd on PD, assigning. I'm oncall in eu-west window, will triage.

Anya: grabbing Slack lead. quick check: are we seeing recent deploys to prober-target? @SRE-Release?

Sanjay: no deploys in last 30m, but prober-runner-3 CPU spiked and queue length jumped on metrics. Looks like fanout/backpressure.

Maria: logs from prober-target show a bunch of `upstream reset by peer` and `502/504` from the telemetry endpoint. snippet: `2026-03-15T10:12:03Z prober-target v2 GET /health -> 504`

Devon: running quick k8s checks
```bash
kubectl -n prober get pods -o wide | grep eu-west
# eu-west-runner-1  Running 3/3   10.0.32.11
# eu-west-runner-2  Running 3/3   10.0.32.12
# eu-west-runner-3  Running 1/3   10.0.32.13  (OOMKilled recently)
```

Anya: eu-west-runner-3 had OOMs and is flapping. That would explain queue backlog and timeouts. Could be a memory regression in the prober process.

Devon: mitigation plan: (1) reduce canary fanout to 1 for eu-west to stop backlog, (2) cordon eu-west-runner-3, (3) restart prober-target pod group, (4) monitor probe success rate. Runbook snippet below.

Devon: runbook commands:
```bash
# patch canary config to reduce concurrency/fanout
kubectl -n prober patch configmap canary-config --type=json -p='[{"op": "replace", "path": "/data/fanout", "value": "1"}]'
# cordon the flapping node/pod
kubectl -n prober delete pod eu-west-runner-3 --grace-period=30
# scale up runner pool temporarily
kubectl -n prober scale deployment prober-runner --replicas=5
```

Sanjay: applying fanout patch now. will post command output when done.

Sanjay: PATCH applied. fanout now 1.

Anya: deleting eu-west-runner-3 pod to let evict and come up fresh.

Maria: restarting prober-target v2 to clear conn pools.

Devon: bumped prober-runner replicas to 5 to drain backlog while we stabilize.

(30s pass)

Maria: success rate improving: failure rate down from 70% -> 12% over the last 90s. Latency median back to baseline.

Devon: monitoring metrics dashboard: probe_success[1m] trending up, errors dropping. Will keep fanout at 1 for 10m then roll back if stable.

Anya: notifying product/CS: brief note - synthetic checks flapped for eu-west; small set of customers might have seen degraded health telemetry; no API customer-facing errors detected.

Devon: marking PD incident as acknowledged and adding notes. PD: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD12345/notes "reduced fanout, restarted runner, scaled replicas; investigating memory regression on prober binary"

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: PagerDuty incident PD12345 acknowledged by Devon.

Anya: handing off to ops-rotation for follow-up and deeper root cause. @ops-rotation, 4h watch requested: keep fanout=1 until memory regression root cause identified and fixed; if stable after 30m, consider gradual rollup to fanout=2.

ops-rotation: taking handoff. Setting alert suppression for this PD to avoid duplicate pages while we watch. Will run a heap dump and capture prober core on eu-west-runner-3 if it OOMs again.

Devon: added TODOs in the incident ticket: capture heap, compare canary binary build vs last known good, run load test locally.

Anya: thanks all. Closing Slack thread for coordination. Will update incident PD when final RCA is available. :pray:

incident-bot: Closing note appended to PD12345: "Mitigation applied, probe success restored to ~95%. Handoff to ops-rotation for RCA and permanent fix."
